Hi Alex / Janelle 

Thanks again for the call today  good discussion and appreciate the context on PHI handling and procurement timelines. Below is a concise post-call recap and the proposed MAP milestone updates specific to Data Handling & Compliance for ACME Health. I attached the MAP draft (ACME_MAP_v1.2.pdf) and the SOC2 scoping spreadsheet for your review.

POST-CALL RECAP (Data handling milestone)
- Objective: Confirm that Redwood can meet ACME Health requirements for PHI/PII, retention, logging, and audit trails before production sign-off.
- Proposed target close date for this milestone: 2026-05-15
- Milestone owner: ACME Health (procurement/legal) + Redwood (security & legal)

MILESTONE: Data handling & compliance (deliverables)
1) Retention policy: customer-aligned retention policy documented  default suggestion: 90 days for logs/payloads (confirmable)
2) Logging & audit trails: per-request audit logs, admin access logs, immutable event logs for investigation
3) Data residency & segregation: US-region hosting for PHI; option for Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed keys
4) PHI/PII controls: encryption at rest + in transit, role-based access controls, optional payload redaction
5) Legal: DPA + BAA to be agreed and signed

Dependencies / Next steps
- Redwood: provide an updated MAP with milestone dates, security checklist, and SOC2 artifacts (attached)  action: Marissa (today)
- ACME: confirm retention window, any required redaction policy, and procurement timeline  action: Alex/Janelle (by 2026-04-12)
- Security workshop: schedule a 60-90 minute technical deep dive for logging, KMS, and audit trails  target week of 2026-04-20

Could you confirm the retention window and whether ACME requires a BAA for this engagement? I put Priyom on copy for legal timing.

Thanks  I'll update the MAP and send the link to the folder.

Best,

Marissa 

Thanks for the detailed recap. A few clarifications from our side so we can mark the MAP accordingly:

1) PHI: Yes, ACME will be handling PHI in scope for this integration. We require a signed BAA prior to any production ingestion.
2) Data residency: All PHI must be stored and processed in US regions only. We prefer customer-managed keys (bring your own key) if possible.
3) Retention: Our legal advises a 90-day default retention for request/response payloads and 1 year for audit logs, unless redaction is used to remove PHI.
4) Audit logs: We need immutable audit trails including request timestamps, redaction status, model/version used, and operator IDs.

Can Rishi confirm that Redwood's logging/audit capability supports immutable trails and that we can push logs to our SIEM (S3/CloudTrail-compatible) with a 1-year retention? Also asking Priyom to advise on the BAA timeline.

We'd like to get the procurement and legal review started this month  can you send an updated MAP reflecting the items above (retention/BAA/KMS) and a short list of required artifacts for our security team?

Appreciate it 
Alex Chen
Director of Platform Integrations | ACME Health

Alex / Marissa 

Thanks for the thread. Quick security confirmation and open items from our side:

Security capabilities (what Redwood supports today)
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments via KMS/HSM integrations; hosted customers can request CMK integration under enterprise contract.
- Audit logs: We can produce immutable, append-only audit logs that capture request timestamp, request id, model id/version, user/operator id, and redaction status. Logs can be exported to an S3 bucket (or S3-compatible endpoint) with options for lifecycle policy to meet 1 year retention.
- Redaction: We offer optional middleware redaction before logs persist; engineering must agree on redaction rules (PII/PHI patterns).
- Access controls: RBAC for consoles and API tokens; elevated access requires explicit approval and is logged.

Open items / dependencies
1) BAA: Priyom will lead a draft BAA; we'll need ACME legal contact for redlines and a target review window.
2) SOC2 artifacts: I've attached a brief security checklist and will pull SOC2 scoping items  these will be available by 2026-04-13.
3) Technical workshop: Recommend a 60-minute session with ACME infra/security to validate KMS flow and log export (deliverable: architecture diagram and config playbook).

I'll attach a short checklist (security-checklist.md) to the shared Drive and drop it in the MAP folder. If ACME prefers a vendor questionnaire, send it over and we'll respond within 3 business days.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
